prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-24. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.92 |
| Retained earnings       | 29,765M |
| Current liabilities     | 3,702M |
| Current assets          | 7,091M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 29,833M |
| Total liabilities       | 21,966M |
| Total assets            | 51,799M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,489M |
| Revenue                 | 5,638M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-24, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided metrics indicate a large, mature company with strong liquidity (current ratio of 1.92), low leverage (total liabilities at only 42% of assets and well below equity), and exceptional profitability (EBIT margin near 44%). These factors, combined with the very large retained-earnings balance, are consistent with upper-tier investment-grade credit quality but fall short of the near-perfect resilience required for AAA.
DECISION: AA-
(The rating uses pre-2026 rating-agency criteria and ratio benchmarks for industrials/utilities; the absence of interest-coverage or cash-flow data prevents a more granular distinction.)
